# 1. Official Dataset Provenance

* **Governing Body:** Department of Hydrology and Meteorology (DHM), Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation, Government of Nepal
* **Official Registry:** DHM National Meteorological and Hydrological Network Directory
* **Administrative Scope:** Gulmi District, Lumbini Province (Province 5), Nepal
* **Classification:** `OBSERVED REAL`
* **Data File:** `data/real/hydrology/gulmi_dhm_stations.geojson`
* **Portal Link:** [DHM Nepal Hydrometric and Climate Portal](https://dhm.gov.np)

# 2. Station Network Inventory

The district of Gulmi features a rigorous network of 8 Department of Hydrology and Meteorology (DHM) monitoring installations spanning from low-altitude river confluences (Ridi Bazar at 494m) to steep mountain ridges (Bharse at 1,626m):

| 241 | **722** | **Musikot** | Precipitation | 1353 | [83.26803, 28.16998] | Musikot | Badigad Watershed | Standard Rain Gauge |

# 3. Scientific Methodology & Integration

The station network monitors two fundamental physical regimes essential to the Water-Energy-Food-Ecosystem Nexus:

1. **Topographic Rainfall Uplift (Orographic Rain Ratio):**
   $$P_{\text{downscaled}}(z) = P_{\text{regional}} \cdot \left[1 + \gamma \cdot (z - z_{\text{ref}})\right]$$
   where $z$ is the elevation of the terrain and $\gamma$ is the empirical mid-hill precipitation lapse rate calibrated against high-ridge stations (Bharse at 1,626m vs Ridi at 494m).

2. **Hydrological River Discharge & Stage-Discharge Rating:**
   $$Q = a \cdot (h - h_0)^b$$
   used for river level telemetry across the Badigad and Panaha river systems.
